title: Prove a five-seat hat wave runs with no panes and drops a late seat by name
action: This slice is PROOF, not construction: the seat name, the 600 second hat clamp and the result drain already live on the herding path and the no-pane runner inherits them (per D11). Do not add new mechanism for any of it — if something is missing, report it rather than building it. Rebuild first and install the binary at .bee/bin/bee, because doctor byte-compares the belt against the compiled copy and a stale vendored binary makes the whole run worthless (this bit pnsd-4: doctor reported binary_freshness not_ok). Then prove four things about a five-seat hat wave where every seat runs as a child process. One: all five seats run in parallel with NO tmux pane opened — count panes before and after with bee herding pane list and assert the count is unchanged, the way pnsd-4 did (26 before, 26 after). Two: every result is named by its seat — assert the seat field on each result envelope matches the seat that was dispatched, and that five distinct seats come back. Three: the wave stays inside its budget. Four, and this is the one that matters most: a seat that exceeds the ceiling is DROPPED AND NAMED, never silently lost. Force it rather than waiting for it — dispatch one seat with a deliberately tiny --ceiling and a task that cannot finish in time, then assert the run returns outcome TimedOutCeiling AND that the result still carries its seat name. The runner kills the child at the ceiling and returns RunOutcome::TimedOutCeiling; confirm the seat survives onto that envelope rather than assuming it does. Record the whole drive as a new sub-feature in pi-hat-wave.md, following that file's existing four-H2 contract, with the exact commands and their assertions.

truths: Five hat seats run as child processes with no tmux pane opened, proven by an unchanged pane count
Every seat's result is named by its seat, and five distinct seats return
A seat that exceeds its ceiling returns TimedOutCeiling and is still named by its seat
The wave stays inside its wall-clock budget

trace.verification_evidence: 576 passed, 0 failed, and the leader independently reproduced D10 crux rather than accepting the worker report. Leader run, from the worktree against the rebuilt binary: printf a long task | bee herding run --no-pane --seat hat-risks --ceiling 1 returned outcome timed_out_ceiling with seat hat-risks and pane_id null, and the pane count was 26 before and 26 after. That is drop-and-name holding on the native path. The worker own drive in a control-bee sandbox reported the other three truths with evidence files: five seats (hat-facts-gaps, hat-alternatives, hat-user-impact, hat-risks, hat-value) each returning outcome done with pane_id null and a report_path, pane count 27 unchanged before during and after, and 12.62 seconds wall clock against a 600 second budget.
